messages:
sam-infra: FYI customer reported Private deployment audit logs stopped showing up in their SIEM this morning. They see local agent producing events but nothing leaves the VPC. Escalating for security review and triage.

lisa-security: Thanks — can you add the customer id and the VPC id? also any recent config changes? :eyes:

sam-infra: cust-2389, vpc-03a7c2. No config changes on our side in the last 48h according to console. Customer says they recently rotated KMS keys yesterday but that is for data-at-rest not logging.

raj-sre: Quick checklist: NAT gateway health, route table default route, outbound ACLs, and any VPC firewall appliance between subnets. Also confirm whether the SIEM uses a public endpoint (https) or a private ingestion endpoint.

marta-ops: Customer says SIEM ingestion is public HTTPS on port 443 (ingest.siem.example.com). I asked for traceroutes; they pasted this: 
```
traceroute to ingest.siem.example.com (54.23.11.9), 30 hops max
 1  10.0.1.1 (10.0.1.1)  0.5 ms
 2  10.10.254.1 (10.10.254.1)  1.1 ms
 3  * * *
```

ian-net: That looks like packets stopping at the firewall/NAT layer. Can we get a tcpdump on a host that runs the logging agent? Capture for destination 54.23.11.9:443 and the KMS endpoint for key service (kms.internal.corp).

sam-infra: Got a pcap from customer, filtered a bit: 
```
15:12:01.123 IP 10.0.2.45.54321 > 54.23.11.9.443: Flags [S], seq 0, win 65535, options [mss 1460], length 0
15:12:01.124 IP 10.0.2.45.54321 > 10.10.254.1.12345: Flags [S], seq 0, win 65535, length 0
no reply
```

lisa-security: Two likely causes: (A) egress blocked by firewall rules (explicit deny) or stateful firewall dropping replies because of asymmetric routing; (B) egress is allowed but outbound proxy requires TLS inspection / SNI allow list and is rejecting. Also KMS rotation might have changed key policy — but that wouldn't stop outbound network.

raj-sre: Can customer confirm route table for subnet 10.0.2.0/24 has 0.0.0.0/0 -> nat-0bcd12 and NAT shows healthy? If they use transit gateways or firewall appliances we need rule snapshot.

marta-ops: Customer says NAT is healthy. They do have a third-party firewall appliance (fw-45) in the path. Showing rules: 
```
rule 100 allow tcp 10.0.0.0/8 any established
rule 200 deny tcp any any eq 443
rule 210 allow tcp 10.0.0.0/8 any eq 443
```

ian-net: Ah — rule 200 denies any->any:443, then rule 210 allows only from 10.0.0.0/8. If source ip is NATed to 100.64.x.x (carrier NAT) or to a different managed IP range, replies will be denied. That would explain traceroute/tcpdump no reply.

sam-infra: Customer confirmed agent host source IP after NAT is 100.64.5.12. They said NAT recent backend change moved to a shared address pool.

lisa-security: For compliance review: we need to document that outbound firewall rules prevented audit log egress, list impacted times, and include mitigation steps. Also validate that no sensitive logs were forwarded elsewhere.

raj-sre: Immediate remediation options: 1) Add explicit allow for NAT egress range to SIEM endpoint (ingest.siem.example.com:443) on fw-45, or 2) SNAT to a stable egress IP in the permitted subnet, or 3) route logging traffic through a dedicated egress VPC with approved egress IPs.

marta-ops: Customer applied rule change to allow 100.64.5.0/24 -> 54.23.11.9:443 and logs started flowing within 3 minutes. They attached the agent logs showing TLS handshake success.

sam-infra: Great. For postmortem and security sign-off we need: timeline, firewall ruleset snapshot before and after, NAT config change ticket, KMS rotation ticket (for completeness), and proof logs reached SIEM (ingest ack).

lisa-security: I'll open a security review issue and request retention/audit copies of the logs for the gap period. Also verify key usage: even though KMS rotation wasn't root cause, confirm that agent encryption/decryption succeeded post-rotation.

incident-bot: Incident record created: INC-2026-1392. Owner: lisa-security. Severity: medium. Affected subsystem: Private VPC audit forwarding.

raj-sre: Adding recommended runbook snippet to avoid reoccurrence: 
```
# runbook excerpt
- Ensure egress IPs used by NAT are pinned or listed in firewall allowlist
- On FW appliances, prefer allowlist by destination + source egress pool
- Monitor agent TLS handshake failure rate > 5/min -> alert
```

sam-infra: Thanks team. I'll coordinate with customer on the runbook changes and provide the artifacts for compliance. Closing the Slack triage once docs are in the incident ticket. :white_check_mark:
